sections.h2: Who handles your Kenton County tax bill
sections.html:
Three offices split the work. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) assigns value. The Kenton County Sheriff mails and collects the bill. The Kenton County Clerk takes over any bill still open after April 15.

The PVA does not set rates, create taxing districts or take payments. Escrow questions and bill questions go to the sheriff. The summer sale and the delinquent lists belong to the clerk. The rate itself comes from the school district, city, county and fire district named on your bill.

The county has two seats, Covington and Independence, and the PVA keeps an office in each. In Covington the office sits at 1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 3300, open weekdays 8:15 to 4:15. The Independence one is at 5272 Madison Pike, open weekdays 8 to 4 and closed from 1 to 2. One number, 859-392-1750, reaches both.

Collection runs from October 1 to April 15. The cheapest window is the first one, which ends November 1 and takes 2 percent off the face amount. Penalties begin in January.

What the sheriff charges, by date paid
Date paidYou owe
Oct. 1 through Nov. 1Bill minus 2 percent
Nov. 2 through Dec. 31Bill as printed
Jan. 1 through Jan. 31Bill plus 5 percent
Feb. 1 through Apr. 15Bill plus 10 percent, then another 10 percent

If April 15 lands on a weekend or holiday, the close moves to the next business day.

You can pay at the sheriff's Covington counter (1840 Simon Kenton Way, Suite 1200) or at the Independence courthouse. Heritage Bank branches accept cash or checks at the window. You can also mail a payment, pay by card or e-check online for a convenience fee, or let your mortgage escrow handle it. A bounced check costs $50.

No bill in hand by October 15? Phone 859-392-1800 and ask the sheriff's office to confirm the amount for your parcel.

sections.h2: The county rate and what else is on the bill
sections.html:
The county's slice is thin. In August 2025 the Fiscal Court voted to lower its real property rate from 12.5 to 11.5 cents per $100 of valuation. That was a fifth straight annual cut and the lowest since 1983. By the county's own example, a home valued at $275,000 pays $316.25 to the county.

The rest of the bill comes from bodies the Fiscal Court does not control: school districts, the health department, the library and fire protection districts. Cities add their own taxes, and Morning View has no city taxes. The sheriff's property tax page has a phone list for city tax collections. For a line-by-line breakdown on one address, call the sheriff.

Your first move is a review request sent to the PVA, which takes them from January 1 onward. It also counts as the mandatory conference that must happen before anything formal.

Conferences run by email or in person by appointment. You can file the Review Request Form online, in person or by phone. The burden of proof sits with you. Check the PVA's supporting documentation list before you gather evidence. Its site also posts sales dashboards and a comparable sales map for houses and condominiums. Nothing is accepted after the inspection period closes.

  • Formal inspection opens the first Monday in May and runs 13 days.
  • The conference period ends at the close of the PVA's business day on the last day of that window, and the filing with the clerk is due shortly after. Check the PVA's posted times each spring.
  • A conference record, Form 62A307, must accompany any filing with the clerk.

The Board of Assessment Appeals is separate from the PVA and runs through the County Clerk's office. A loss there can go to the Kentucky Board of Tax Appeals, which answers to neither the PVA nor any taxing authority.

The PVA follows a four-year review plan, so every parcel gets a physical look at least that often. Owners in Elsmere, Erlanger, Fort Mitchell, Lakeside Park and Park Hills may see inspectors working their areas, and the PVA lists the sales behind its re-evaluations for Bromley, Covington and Ludlow. The office also values about 5,000 commercial and industrial properties and prices motor vehicles at January 1 using NADA figures.

A homestead reduction is open to owners turning 65 within the year, filed through the PVA's online application. Owners who are totally disabled may also claim it. It follows the owner, not the property, which means a buyer must file a new application. Business personal property returns are due May 15, with no relief from a tax filing extension.

Once April 15 passes, the sheriff stops and the Kenton County Clerk picks up the file. Your unpaid bill is converted into a certificate of delinquency carrying a lien, and fees plus 1 percent interest each month keep adding up.

The clerk holds a yearly sale in July. A bill still open then can be sold to an outside buyer, and redeeming it costs substantially more. State revenue officials show the climb with a $1,000 example: $1,254 on transfer and roughly $1,388 if paid at the clerk's counter within five business days, before the county attorney's fee applies.

  • The county attorney's first notice goes out in the month after transfer.
  • A newspaper ad and a website list name the delinquent parcels ahead of the sale.
  • Expect the sale between 90 and 135 days after the clerk gets the file.

Before listing, pay off any old certificate so nothing jumps out at closing. Have the clerk put a payoff figure on paper, then pass it to your title company.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill at closing
sections.html:
After you sell, the next bill can still carry your name, or both names. The sheriff explains that the seller credits their share to the buyer or escrow agent at closing, and the owner of record then pays the whole bill. Before you close, confirm which year's bill is still unpaid and make sure the title company has the sheriff's current figure.

A cash sale skips the lender's escrow analysis and the usual wait on a buyer's loan, so the tax proration is a single line on the settlement statement. Bring the latest bill, any delinquent notice and your PVA exemption paperwork to the closing table.

sections.h2: Kenton County housing at a glance
sections.html: Kenton is the third most populous county in Kentucky, with an estimated 175,779 residents in July 2025. It holds 74,593 housing units, and 70.7 percent of households own. The median home value is $244,400, and median gross rent is $1,069. Five school districts serve the county, from dense northern cities to rural southern areas, so tax bills on similar houses can differ by district.

faqs.q: When are Kenton County property tax bills due?
faqs.a: Pay by November 1 for the 2 percent discount. Face amount is due through December 31, penalties begin January 1 and the sheriff stops on April 15.

faqs.q: Where do I pay my Kenton County property tax?
faqs.a: At the sheriff's Covington or Independence counters, a Heritage Bank branch, by mail to P.O. Box 188070 in Erlanger, online, or through mortgage escrow.

faqs.q: Who do I call if my Kenton County tax bill is wrong?
faqs.a: The PVA at 859-392-1750 handles value and exemptions. The sheriff handles the bill itself, and the PVA neither collects nor sets rates.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Kenton County assessment?
faqs.a: Request a PVA conference inside the 13-day May inspection window. The clerk filing is due one working day after the window closes.

faqs.q: What is the Kenton County property tax rate?
faqs.a: The Fiscal Court lowered its real property rate to 11.5 cents per $100 in August 2025. School, city, library, health and fire levies are billed on top.
